_comment: Hand-calculated, not copied from any program output.
Matches PO-1 (S1, CAB-1, ordered_quantity=5, unit_cents=2000) and
its receipt RC-1 (received_quantity=5).
expected_cents = ordered_quantity * unit_cents = 5 * 2000 = 10000
billed_cents = total_cents on the invoice = 8 * 2000 = 16000
difference_cents = billed_cents - expected_cents = 16000 - 10000 = 6000
billed_quantity (8) != ordered_quantity (5) and != received_quantity (5),
so the quantity-mismatch rule applies: status is 'discrepant' regardless
of the sign or size of difference_cents (domain.md step 5).
Discrepant invoices are not duplicates and not unresolved, so nothing
here excludes it from a recoverable total on that basis.
Hand-calculated, not copied from any program output.
Matches PO-2 (S1, CAB-1, ordered_quantity=5, unit_cents=2000) and
its receipt RC-2 (received_quantity=5).
expected_cents = ordered_quantity * unit_cents = 5 * 2000 = 10000
billed_cents = total_cents on the invoice = 5 * 1800 = 9000
difference_cents = billed_cents - expected_cents = 9000 - 10000 = -1000
billed_quantity (5) equals both ordered_quantity (5) and received_quantity (5),
so the quantity-mismatch rule does NOT apply. difference_cents is non-zero,
so status is 'discrepant' (domain.md: 'a non-zero difference -- positive or
negative -- is discrepant'). This is the undercharge case: a negative
difference_cents, which the supplied rules do not separately name but do not
exempt from 'discrepant' either.
This result must be EXCLUDED from any recoverable-amount total: the task
brief directs that an undercharge (negative difference) is excluded from
recoverable amounts even though its status is discrepant, same as an
overcharge. This is the one place this fixture set encodes a decision
beyond a literal reading of domain.md -- recorded here, not silently
assumed.
